items.headline: Singaporean man, 24, jailed 17 years with caning for sexually abusing his half-sister
items.summary: A 24-year-old man was sentenced on 12 November to 17 years' jail and 24 strokes of the cane for repeatedly sexually assaulting his younger half-sister and for filming women in the shower; the abuse came to light after his arrest for voyeurism.

items.headline: Father and son flew from China to Singapore to assault a Malaysian man over a failed investment
items.summary: A father and son were each jailed 10 weeks after travelling from China to confront and assault a Malaysian man over a failed S$18,000 investment; both pleaded guilty.

items.headline: Singapore courts to weigh reformative training or jail by default for young scam offenders
items.summary: Under a sentencing framework debated in Parliament, courts will consider reformative training or imprisonment as the default for young offenders drawn into scams, reflecting the harm caused by syndicates.

items.headline: Singaporean man, 20, jailed seven years with caning for sex with three underage girls
items.summary: A 20-year-old man was sentenced to seven years' jail and six strokes of the cane for having sex with three underage girls, one of whom is deaf and unable to speak.

items.headline: India bypassed its own 'Make in India' rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tools
items.summary: An Internet Freedom Foundation investigation reported by Al Jazeera says Home Minister Amit Shah signed exemptions letting state forensic labs buy at least 422 foreign products, including Cellebrite phone-hacking kit from Israel, sidestepping domestic-procurement rules.

items.headline: Trump's midterm setback revives hopes for a US-India trade deal by year-end
items.summary: CNBC reports that with US-India negotiations largely complete, officials see a trade pact possibly signed around the December G20 summit; a US Supreme Court ruling against Trump's tariffs has given New Delhi more leverage.

items.headline: India's asset-management industry presses New Delhi to scrap capital-gains tax on foreign investors
items.summary: After about US$49 billion of foreign equity outflows, India's roughly US$900 billion asset-management industry and its market regulator are urging the government to drop the 12.5% long-term capital-gains tax for foreign investors; Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said she would consider it.

items.headline: UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest pace in years
items.summary: Official data showed UK GDP expanded 0.7% in the third quarter, led by services and what Chancellor John Healey called an AI-driven 'extra engine of growth'; analysts said a December Bank of England rate rise remains likely, with markets pricing about a 73% chance.

items.headline: Britain refuses to adopt EU AI rules, complicating a post-Brexit reset
items.summary: The UK government said it will not accept the European Union's artificial-intelligence rules as a condition of closer ties, deepening a regulatory split as London and Brussels prepare for a summit.

items.headline: Burnham warns of 'long nights ahead' as a UK-EU summit looms
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told colleagues to expect 'long nights ahead' over the coming week as his government negotiates a reset of relations with the European Union.

items.headline: Update: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner meet Putin in Moscow and agree to keep Ukraine talks going
items.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on 12 November; the Kremlin called the talks useful and both sides agreed to continue direct negotiations, days after US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a territorial breakthrough. Kyiv again rejected ceding the Donbas.

items.headline: Trump's 'Board of Peace' rebukes Israel over its response to Gaza flooding
items.summary: The Trump-created Board of Peace called Israel's response to weekend flooding in Gaza 'insufficient' and urged it to allow in shelter and sanitation supplies; the UN says Israeli strikes have killed more than 1,400 people in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire.

items.headline: UN chief says 'the climate crisis is outrunning us' as COP31 bargains in Turkey
items.summary: At the COP31 summit in Antalya, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged a phase-out of coal, oil and gas and accused the fossil-fuel lobby of delaying action, as producer nations resisted; the United States skipped the talks for a second year.

items.headline: European leaders meet in Dublin as drone and 'hybrid' attacks dominate security talks
items.summary: Leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin on 12 November focused on regional security amid a wave of drone incursions and sabotage blamed on Russia; Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy attended and was due to meet US envoys.

items.headline: Update: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns as CFO Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis
items.summary: Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as chief executive, president and director effective immediately, after a scandal over an alleged affair tied to a suspected Chinese-intelligence approach; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO and Harvey Jones is named the company's first board chair. Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% before paring losses.

items.headline: OpenAI raises about US$15 billion at a US$1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: CNBC reported that OpenAI raised roughly US$15 billion in its latest round at a US$1.25 trillion valuation, about half its original US$30 billion target, as it keeps funding data-centre spending ahead of a planned 2027 IPO.

items.headline: Anthropic sets an IPO price range of US$70 to US$78, implying a US$1.4 trillion valuation
items.summary: Anthropic set an indicative IPO price range of US$70 to US$78 per share, which would value the Claude maker at an implied US$1.404 trillion, in one of the largest technology listings on record.

items.headline: Norwest raises a US$4 billion fund to push deeper into AI
items.summary: The Wells Fargo-backed firm Norwest closed a US$4 billion fund as it steps up investment in artificial-intelligence startups, among the larger venture vehicles raised this year.

items.headline: Cisco beats estimates and says AI-infrastructure revenue will double this year
items.summary: Cisco reported fiscal first-quarter adjusted earnings of US$1.40 a share on US$18.5 billion in revenue, both above forecasts, and raised its expected AI-infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to about US$9 billion this fiscal year; shares rose after hours.

items.headline: Gold slips below US$4,000 to a one-week low as bets on a December Fed hike firm
items.summary: Spot gold fell for a third session to around US$3,931 an ounce as a stronger dollar and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary lifted rate-hike expectations; traders now price an 89% chance of a quarter-point US rate increase in December.

items.headline: Wall Street slips as Nvidia's leadership shock rattles the AI trade
items.summary: US stocks eased on 12 November, with the S&P 500 down about 0.35% to 7,592 and the Nasdaq off 0.39%, as Nvidia initially plunged 14% on Jensen Huang's resignation before halving the loss.

items.headline: Soaring OpenAI and Anthropic valuations stir investor fears of an AI startup correction
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that record private valuations for OpenAI and Anthropic are fuelling venture-capital concern about a possible correction, as some funding rounds come in below earlier targets.

items.headline: 🎾 Andreeva routs Sabalenka to reach her first WTA Finals semifinal
items.summary: Mirra Andreeva, 19, recovered from 4-1 down in the first set to beat world No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 in Indian Wells on 11 November, topping her group to reach her first WTA Finals semifinal.

items.headline: 🎾 Svitolina rallies past Muchova to stay alive at the WTA Finals
items.summary: Elina Svitolina came from a set down to beat Karolina Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, keeping her semifinal hopes alive before a decider against Aryna Sabalenka.

items.headline: 🏏 Pakistan press for victory over Sri Lanka in the Rawalpindi Test
items.summary: Pakistan held the upper hand as the first Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi moved toward its final day, leading by 45 runs in the second innings after Sri Lanka's reply of 446 featured an unbeaten 249-run stand between Dhananjaya and Kusal.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1's final triple-header opens in Las Vegas with the runner-up fight still live
items.summary: With Kimi Antonelli already crowned the 2026 champion on 390 points, Formula 1 heads to the Las Vegas Grand Prix on 19-21 November to open its closing triple-header; Max Verstappen holds second on 279 points, 17 clear of Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

items.headline: Europe's Euclid telescope releases a trove mapping more than a billion cosmic objects
items.summary: ESA's Euclid mission published its first major cosmology data release, DR1-Foundation, covering the light of more than a billion objects, including over 900 million galaxies, about 15,000 strong-lensing candidates and 60 million quasar candidates, from 13 months of observations.

items.headline: A burst of two genes helps mouse hearts regenerate after a heart attack
items.summary: In Nature Cardiovascular Research, researchers used a transient, modified-mRNA dose of the genes Myc and cyclin T1 to make adult heart-muscle cells divide in mice after a heart attack, reducing scar tissue and improving function; sustained expression proved harmful, underscoring the need for a brief, targeted pulse.

items.headline: Global wildlife trade involves about 107,000 species, more than double past estimates
items.summary: A study highlighted in Nature finds roughly 107,000 species are traded worldwide, legally or illegally, more than twice the previous estimate, reshaping the picture of trade's pressure on biodiversity.

items.headline: A new obesity definition based on organ function outperforms BMI
items.summary: An international study of 844,108 adults, reported in Nature, found that a framework distinguishing clinical from preclinical obesity by body measures and organ dysfunction classified obesity and predicted mortality risk better than body-mass-index criteria.

fun_fact.headline: The dot over an i or j is called a tittle
fun_fact.body: The dot over a lowercase ‘i’ or ‘j’ has its own name: a tittle. The word comes from the Latin titulus, the same root behind ‘title’; the phrase ‘to a T’ may even trace back to ‘to a tittle,’ meaning precise to the smallest mark.

puzzle.title: Running Home
puzzle.body:
A man was running home. Partway there, he saw a masked man standing in his path, so he stopped, turned, and ran back the way he came.

Where was the man running, and who was the masked man?
puzzle.approach: Picture the scene literally, then ask what ‘home’ and a ‘masked man’ could both be.
puzzle.answer:
He is a baseball player.

‘Home’ is home plate, and the man is a base runner trying to score. Seeing the catcher — the ‘masked man’ guarding the plate — ready to tag him out, he reversed and ran back toward third base to avoid being put out.

word_puzzle.title: The Anagram Trio
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange every letter of each phrase into the answer described:

1.  DIRTY ROOM  →  a place to sleep (9 letters)
2.  THEY SEE  →  what you see with (3, 4)
3.  ELEVEN PLUS TWO  →  another way to write 13 (6, 4, 3)
word_puzzle.approach: Each clue’s letters rearrange exactly into the answer — none added, none left over.
word_puzzle.answer:
1.  DIRTY ROOM  =  DORMITORY
2.  THEY SEE  =  THE EYES
3.  ELEVEN PLUS TWO  =  TWELVE PLUS ONE

Each answer uses exactly the same letters as its clue — a perfect anagram. (ELEVEN PLUS TWO and TWELVE PLUS ONE even both equal 13.)
